newsitem.title: USA: NEES gets proposals from 25 companies.
newsitem.headline: NEES gets proposals from 25 companies.

text.p: New England Electric System said Wednesday it has received preliminary proposals for the purchase of its generation business from 25 potential buyers.
It said the proposals, received on March 21, are from utility affiliates, independent power producers and energy companies, both domestic and international.

Some were for the business as a whole and others were for portions of the business. Many companies submitted multiple proposals, NEES said. It is the parent of Massachusetts Electric Co, Narragansett Electric Co, Granite State Electric Co and New England Power Co.
"We are encouraged by the caliber of the companies that expressed interest, and the quality of the proposals," chief executive John W. Rowe said.
"While we are far from completing the sale, the initial proposals confirm the view that divestiture will reduce stranded investment and increase savings for consumers."

NEES said its subsidiaries and their financial advisor, Merrill Lynch & Co, have reviewed the preliminary proposals and Wednesday invited a select group to submit formal, binding bids by the end of June.
The undisclosed finalists were selected based on an assessment of which bids would most reduce the stranded cost access charges to be paid by customers, NEES said.

Based on the proposals received, it said, bids will be requested for three options: the non-nuclear generation business as a whole; the fossil fuel plants together with the purchased power contracts; and the hydroelectric business consisting of the conventional hydro plants and the Bear Swamp pumped storage hydro facility.
"We decided to release this description of our progress because of the intense interest and speculation around our divestiture," Rowe said.
"We hope to be announcing a purchase and sale agreement by mid-year and to complete the sale in mid-1998 after the necessary regulatory approvals have been received.
"We cannot disclose more detail because to do so could compromise our ability to maximize the value we obtain for our business."

NEES is selling 4,000 megawatts of fossil and hydro capacity including three fossil-fueled plants, a pumped storage hydro plant, and the region's largest renewable portfolio consisting of 14 hydroelectric facilities, as well as 1,150 megawatts of purchased power contracts.
NEES will also attempt to sell its minority interests in four nuclear plants, which represent an additional 500 megawatts of capacity, in a separate sale process.
